title: Grid Multi-Word Search
statement:
Find every word from a list that can be traced in a letter grid.

Contract
- `grid` is a non-empty rectangular array of lowercase letters; `words` holds non-empty lowercase words and may contain duplicates.
- A word can be traced when its letters can be read along a path of cells, each step moving to an up, down, left, or right neighbour. A single cell may not be used twice within the same word, but different words may reuse cells.
- Return each traceable word exactly once, in any order. Return an empty list when nothing can be traced.
- The grid may be changed during the search, but it must hold its original letters when the method returns.

Examples
- For the grid `cat / ors / den` and words `cat, cod, care, dog`, the result is `cat`, `cod`, `care` (any order); `dog` has no `g` to use.
- For the grid `ab` and the word `aba`, the result is empty because the only `a` would be used twice.
- For the grid `x` and the words `x, x`, the result is just `x`.
hints: Searching the grid once per word repeats a lot of work. Put all the words into a trie so one search from each cell serves every word at once.

Run a depth-first search from every cell, following only letters that continue a prefix in the trie, and mark the current cell as used (then restore it) so a word never reuses a cell. Stop a branch as soon as the trie has no matching child.

Clear a word from the trie once it is found so it is reported once. Intended complexity: with a fixed word list of bounded length, each cell starts a bounded search, so time is O(n) where n is the number of grid cells; extra space is O(1) beyond the trie and the result.
inputSyntax: Input: grid rows separated by commas, then ';' and the words separated by commas, for example: cat,ors,den; cat,cod,care
